subject: cardboardRobot
pitch:
Category: Humanoid character.
Subject: kid in a cardboard-box robot costume.
Style: cardboard craft.
reasoning:
I'm planning a kid-sized robot costume made from a cardboard box, with a face window in the helmet, foil-wrapped limb tubes, buttons, dials, antennae, and marker/duct-tape details, aiming to keep the scene around 150 parts for efficiency.

Now I'm working out the skeleton: hips, a two-joint spine chain, neck, head, jaw, arm chains (shoulder/elbow/wrist), and leg chains (hip/knee/ankle), with an A-pose rest stance. I'm roughing out proportions for a ~1.15-1.3 m child wearing the box costume, then placing the head sphere and an oversized box helmet around it, figuring out how to represent a face opening since true cutouts aren't possible.

Instead I'm building the helmet from separate frame panels (top, bottom, left, right bars) leaving a rectangular window in front so the inner head is visible, and working out the exact dimensions and y-ranges for the helmet box, head sphere, neck cylinder, and torso box so everything lines up with the legs starting around y=0.5.

Now I'm adjusting the torso box height and shoulder positions, then plotting the kid's arm sweep from shoulder to elbow to wrist with foil-tube sleeves and red glove hands, and setting up hip-knee-ankle coordinates for the legs with thicker foil tube limbs.

Shoes become small red sneaker boxes at the ankles, with shorts covering the upper legs and skin showing just above. I'm setting up a mirror loop for left/right symmetry, naming joints like "shoulderL" and "shoulderR", then building catmull-rom chains for the arms (shoulder-elbow-wrist) and legs (hip-knee-ankle) parented to the spine and hips respectively.

Now I'm sweeping tubes along those chains for limb geometry with rounded caps, attaching foot boxes to the ankle joint, and designing custom textures -- a corrugated cardboard paint with stripe noise, a crinkly foil paint using mottled grays instead of importing an external kit, and planning an SVG robot face with dials and buttons for the chest panel.

I'm also sketching out a decal system for a hidden kid's face on the skull with simple eyes and a smile, plus marker-style doodles like hazard tape, scribbles, and a gear sketch on the back, and wiring up glow textures for the antenna bulb and chest lights using the glow kit. Now I'm positioning the textured chest plane just in front of the torso surface so it sits flush against the body.

Writing box part and cardboard paint logic...

Working out the flap rotation math...

Confirming the flap rotation sign resolves correctly and won't collide with the helmet or head, then I'm laying out the helmet's panel structure—top, back, and side boxes plus front frame bars—positioning each relative to the head bone's dimensions.

Shaping the hair as a partial sphere covering the upper skull, tilted back to expose the face, with small boxes for bangs, and adding a separate jaw piece attached near the jaw joint.

Now I'm positioning the jaw as a scaled sphere beneath the skull, then placing decal textures for the eyes and mouth directly onto the skull surface using forward-facing decals, deciding whether the mouth should sit on the skull or move down onto the jaw part instead.

I'll settle on using the skull surface for all three facial decals, with the jaw sphere positioned just under the chin. For the helmet, I'm adding antennae as thin rods topped with glowing bulbs, plus cylindrical "toilet-paper tube" ears on the sides for a playful robot-costume look, skipping other extras like a dryer hose.

For torso decoration, I'm planning a chest panel with glowing control buttons, a hazard-striped band at the torso's base, a gear doodle on the back, and corner duct-tape strips crossing the seams, while skipping a slinky-style hose detail. I'm also repositioning the arm attachment points so the foil sleeve starts properly at the torso's side rather than floating outside the box.

Now I'm adding elbow joints and cuffs along the arm chain, using tangent-aligned cylinders for the elbow rings and red tape bands, then finishing each arm with a sphere-based mitten hand to suggest a kid's yellow dishwashing glove as a costume detail.

For the lower body, I'm sketching blue jean shorts as a small box at the hip, mostly hidden behind the cardboard but peeking through slightly, then building out red sneaker shoes at the foot with a white sole box and a toe cap sphere positioned near the ankle joint.

Now I'm defining the leg as a tapered sweep from hip to ankle, using a chain of points with varying radii to shape the thigh down to the foot, parented to the hips with left/right sides mirrored by x-position.

For the arm, I'm adding a yellow glove at the wrist tip with a simple mitten shape plus a thumb sphere, skipping detailed individual fingers for simplicity. Then I'm setting up the spine as a catmull-rom chain from hips through two upper points, parented to the hips joint, and figuring out where the neck joint should attach relative to the second spine segment.

Now I'm placing the neck joint parented to the spine, with the head joint above it and a jaw joint parented to the head, each tagged with their role. For the skin, I'm adding a neck capsule rod connecting the neck to the head base, bound to the neck bone.

For facial textures, I'm sketching SVG assets: an eye with a dark ellipse and highlights, a smiling mouth with a tooth gap, and blush/freckle decals using simple circles layered onto the face.

Now I'm working out hair geometry: a cap sphere positioned near the skull center with a limited theta range so it covers the top and back without wrapping the whole head, rotated slightly forward to raise the hairline, plus small spike tufts on top for texture, all in brown.

Next I'm placing small sphere ears on either side of the head, checking whether they'd end up hidden under the hair or the helmet's side panels, and adjusting their position so they poke out appropriately.

I'm also planning decorative touches for the helmet: a small "BOT-9" sticker on the front bar, button-like cylinders on the side tubes, and maybe a gear doodle plane on the back facing outward.

For the chest panel I'm sketching a hand-drawn marker style design — a waveform screen, dials, buttons, and a hazard bar outlined in wobbly black on white paper glued to the cardboard, plus lightning bolt and arrow doodles on the side planes.

Now I'm adding small physical details to the torso: grey duct tape strips crossing the top front seam corners, a hazard-striped tape band lower on the chest, and a trio of glowing cylinder buttons positioned near the panel to match the drawn design.

I'm also working out the antenna assembly—thin silver rods on each side topped with small glowing spheres (red or green) at the tip, bringing the total figure height to around 1.46 including the antenna.

Now I'm considering torso depth details, keeping the kid's body mostly hidden inside the box, and adding small decorative touches like cardboard fold-seam lines, flap edges, and dark rounded handle-hole cutouts on the sides to make the box look more authentic. For the chest texture, I'm sketching an SVG with a paper-colored background bordered in dark outline and a dark green screen panel inset near the top.

Writing texture SVGs...

Adding a "DO NOT OPEN" label and a lightning bolt side decal, then placing eye and nose decals on the skull with proper positioning and scale. I'm also setting up shared material colors and importing a glow helper, plus defining box/shape helper functions for building the model.

Now I'm working out helmet scuffs and tape details with mottled foil paint textures, then moving to limb construction—figuring out hand placement by offsetting sphere positions from the wrist and arm tip coordinates.

Still placing joint details...

I'm skipping shorts for now but adding a small hips bone box to bridge the legs, verifying the sole sits flush at y=0, and making sure the torso box and spine bone align so decals inherit weights automatically. Helmet flaps can be skipped, maybe just a small antenna base added later.
